Honestly unless you plan on using it for large game I'd recommend the Hatsan .30 cal, there are a lot less things to go wrong with a springer or gas piston than a precharged pneumatic, they're usually lighter and weighted better, and with an springer you might be able to fabricate some seals if needed as they should only have one or two, whereas just the cheapest Chinese pump I could buy for my precharged has I believe fourteen synthetic seals or something ridiculous like that. But from personal experience a cheap old spring piston with leather seals can last a lifetime with the original parts and no need for maintenance other than when you want to start using it again.

It's obviously not all roses with a spring piston gun either of course, you're never going to find one that enables you to have a follow up shot as that would require having a second piston assembly, they have a two stage recoil that destroys scopes and your accuracy unless you use an artillery hold, and quite a bit of noise from the piston assembly that can't be muffled with a suppressor there are a few more minor things as well but those are the major drawbacks.

In defense of the Benjamin though it has it's own perks, such as the magazine, most likely better accuracy due to the minimal mechanical movement, the ability to fire multiple shots without having to reload or pump, the extra stopping power, and it just has normal single stage recoil that won't ruin scopes or necessitate and artillery hold. but you'd get all that and more with a powder rifle and it would have less points of failure so the only real appeal would be if you live somewhere with bullet rationing like Oregon and don't already have a stockpile.
Have you ever tried a see all scope on a spring piston? It looks pretty simple and durable and you don't really need any magnification at such short ranges.

For a spring or gas ram gun I'd stay .22 or below, by the time you get a spring power plant that can fire .30 at any reasonable velocity it'll be kicking like a mule and quite hard to shoot. quarterbore and up are only really any good for PCP, and PCP is somewhat less than practical for a long term survival situation.

Whatever you get make sure the barrel is compatible with cast bullets if that's what you intend to use, some (many, most?) aren't. I settled for stockpiling pellets instead.

Finally, don't believe a word that any manufacturer says about FPS. If they give an FPS figure i'll offer you a bet that they're lying, the good ones will only give foot-pounds energy not feet per second.
